newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Mir commander not well enough to do repairs.
newsitem.headline: Mir commander not well enough to do repairs.

text.p: The commander of the Mir space station Vasily Tsibliyev is not well enough to take part in a complex repair operation, a senior Russian space official said on Tuesday.

"We already understand that the commander cannot do this work because of his medical condition," Mikhail Sinelshchikov, head of the Russian Space Agency's manned flight division, told Reuters. He said the decision was not final but added: "There are two options, either it is done by the board engineer and (U.S. astronaut Michael) Foale...or put off to the next crew," Sinelshchikov said.

Solovyov said earlier that NASA's representative at Mission Control outside Moscow had spoken to Foale, who saw no problem in taking Tsibliyev's place for the repairs to Mir's power supply if necessary.
Tsibliyev was to have manned the air lock between the main station and the damaged Spektr module while engineer Alexander Lazutkin undertook the risky and complex repair.

Sinelshchikov said Tsibilyev's irregular heart beat, which showed up in tests on Sunday, was mainly due to tension after Spektr was holed on June 25 in the worst accident in the station's 11-year-history.
"It's not an illness of the heart, but a reaction of the heart to all the pressure," Sinelshchikov said.
